clauses.clause: sec. 1: definitions (Director, affected agencies, arms control, related matters); no independent command
sec. 2: Director and affected agency heads keep each other informed; unresolved major policy differences referred to the President, with notice
sec. 3: Director establishes coordination procedures and leads resolution of differences
sec. 4: Director keeps a research program and inventory and periodically submits a consolidated schedule to the Budget Bureau (Office of Management and Budget after EO 12608)
sec. 5: Secretary of Defense keeps Director informed of force and armament planning; Director furnishes arms control policy statements

propositions.claim: The held text is the Federal Register printing of EO 11044, signed August 20, 1962.
propositions.quote: Executive Order 11044 INTERAGENCY COORDINATION OF ARMS CONTROL AND DISARMAMENT MATTERS

propositions.claim: Sec. 1 defines Director as the Director of ACDA.
propositions.quote: The word “ Director” means the Director of the United States Arms Control and Disarmament Agency.

propositions.claim: Sec. 2 imposes a continuing duty to keep each other informed.
propositions.quote: The Director and the heads o f affected agencies shall keep each other fully and currently informed

propositions.claim: Sec. 3 directs the Director to establish coordination procedures.
propositions.quote: The Director shall establish pro­cedures consistent with this order and the Arms Control and Disarma­ment A ct to assure coordination

propositions.claim: Sec. 4 imposes a continuing research-program duty.
propositions.quote: the Director shall develop and keep current a comprehensive and balanced program of research, development and other studies

propositions.claim: Sec. 5 imposes a continuing duty on the Secretary of Defense.
propositions.quote: The Secretary o f Defense shall keep the Director informed with respect to the planning of armed forces levels and armaments

propositions.claim: EO 12608 (1987) lists 11044 among orders amended to replace Bureau of the Budget references with Office of Management and Budget; a technical amendment, not a revocation.
propositions.quote: by deleting the word “Bureau” and inserting in lieu thereof “O ffice” wherever the word "Bureau” is used as a reference to the Office of Management and Budget: 8248 10903 11044

propositions.claim: The OFR codification page records only the sec. 4 amendment by EO 12608 and no revocation (as of the 1989 codification).
propositions.quote: Sec. 4 amended by Executive Order 12608 of Sept. 9, 1987, 52 FR 34617, 3 CFR, 1987 Comp., p. 245

propositions.claim: ACDA, whose Director is the order's main actor, was abolished by statute (Pub. L. 105-277, div. G, sec. 1211), which does not name EO 11044: a candidate ending only.
propositions.quote: The United States Arms Control and Disarmament Agency is abolished.

propositions.claim: The abolition took effect not later than April 1, 1999.
propositions.quote: shall take effect on the earlier of— (1) April 1, 1999; or (2) the date of abolition

propositions.claim: The same Act's savings provision continues existing orders tied to transferred functions until changed, which cuts against treating abolition as an ending of the order.
propositions.quote: shall continue in effect according to their terms until modified, terminated, superseded, set aside, or revoked

review.conclusion_reason: OPEN is justified because no reviewed source establishes a qualifying ending or positively establishes EO 11044's operation at the cutoff. Formal status is upheld only as the bounded finding that no express ending was found. The applicable basis is the project's OPEN rule, despite the result's uninformative basis_rule value 'none'.
missed_evidence: 22 U.S.C. 6512, https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/22/6512, expressly transfers all ACDA and Director functions to the Secretary of State, including functions 'under any statute, reorganization plan, Executive order, or other provision of law'. Read together with section 6615(a), this resolves the basic succession question against treating agency abolition itself as an ending. It does not independently prove this particular order's cutoff status.
review.stop_code_verdict: wrong (NOT_FOUND fits the remaining cutoff-evidence gap). The project rules already prohibit inferring an ending from a general statute that does not name the order; the evidence slice supplies only a technical amendment and historical codification. Section 6512 supplies the previously unread transfer text. No owner ruling is necessary to retain OPEN pending an order-specific current source or qualifying ending.

verdicts.reason: Held Federal Register OCR identifies EO 11044 and includes Kennedy's signature and August 20, 1962 date.
Section 1(a) contains the quoted ACDA Director definition.
Section 2 requires mutual, fully current information and also contains referral and notice duties.
Section 3(a) requires coordination procedures; subsection (b) separately requires leadership in resolving differences.
Section 4 requires a current research program, continuing inventory, agency advice, and periodic consolidated submissions.
Section 5 imposes the quoted Defense information duty and reciprocal Director policy statements.
Held EO 12608 section 2 lists 11044 for Budget Bureau terminology amendments; section 1's revocation list does not include it.
The Archives page contains the exact section 4 amendment note and no revocation annotation. This supports the historical codification claim, not cutoff status.
The cited section abolishes ACDA and identifies section 1211 of Public Law 105-277; it does not name EO 11044. Abolition alone is not an established ending under the project rules.
The effective-date note gives the earlier-of formula quoted and identifies April 1, 1999 as the abolition date.

Section 6615(a) preserves qualifying presidential orders concerning transferred functions that were effective at the transition, until lawfully changed. The worker correctly treats this as counterevidence rather than conclusive cutoff proof.
